items.transcript: This might be the coolest thing you've seen today. These glasses right here can supposedly read the words that you're like silently mouthing and type them at over 200 words per minute. Now, people typically type around 40 words per minute, so that's a pretty big jump. These are from Subvocal, a tiny Y Combinator startup founded by two Georgia Tech University students. The glasses send radar signals through your face, and then their AI turns the tiny movements from your lips and jaws into text. In the demo, the guy silently asks his AI to summarize his Slack messages for him right next to his coworkers, and nobody knows he's even talking. They're even saying that two people that are wearing these glasses could have a private conversation from across the room with each other without anybody even realizing they're talking. Like real life telepathy. And Apple clearly thinks that this concept is a pretty big deal, too, because earlier this year they paid $1.6 billion for a company that created very similar tech. And these guys right here are already taking pre-orders for 499 bucks. Now, it's still a prototype, and I haven't seen anybody else like independently test their speed claims yet.
